# Match the desktop graphics backend for retained-world startup

The promotional city's approved lighting candidate passed its real isolated
check in 2420 ms but repeatedly failed normal adoption with `Godot runtime
did not report ready`. The old formal world was retained. Extending the
30-second readiness limit would not explain that discrepancy.

The investigation used the exclusive, idle `test-results/pcity` fixture through
its ordinary author lock and native application coordinator. No authored
source or immutable artifact changed, and no source export was repeated.

Evidence under `test-results/pcity/test-results/`:

- `desktop-native-codex-live-AVjcII/operation-error.json` reproduces the original
  failure. Original `dA7He9` and `P9PVXb` failures remain intact.
- `desktop-native-codex-live-rDQHhd/operation-error.json` records more than 1600
  compositor paints with throttling disabled, while a bounded page probe timed
  out. Moving the pending view above the formal view, a separate hidden native
  owner, throttling/detaching the old view, and stopping its offscreen painting
  did not resolve startup. These changes were removed.
- `desktop-native-codex-live-CDHkSK/diagnostic-check-alone.json` records the same
  existing, hash-verified lighting artifacts ready in 2668 ms. In the same
  helper with the old formal city loaded, `diagnostic-check-with-formal.json`
  records a 30-second verifier timeout. These are read-only artifact diagnostics,
  not new Core check registrations. The renderer processes were distinct and
  both had normal OS priority. WebGL initialized before the stall; the last
  console line alone had obscured that fact.
- A temporary profiler attempt also stalled and its helper was explicitly
  retired (`desktop-native-codex-live-1gn037/unexpected-exit.json`). It is not a
  successful application or an identified driver stack. Core restart recovery
  interrupted the uncommitted preparation. No profiler remains in the product.

The live helper uniquely disabled hardware acceleration and forced SwiftShader.
Removing those overrides aligns it with the actual desktop, while keeping
offscreen rendering and every permission/adoption assertion. The identical
lighting candidate then passed preview, a fresh native application preparation,
runner snapshot confirmation, Core commit and formal promotion. The evidence
supports a concurrent startup failure in the forced software configuration;
it does not establish a particular internal SwiftShader/Godot lock.

`desktop-native-codex-live-usVTUF/operation.json` records the successful native
application of candidate
`gcan-58489f4397dfd7403f7215f3f17fbd930ee367a699b997d1103a35cc61f32270`
to formal build
`gbd-b7d6be84679c6645446c0434778bf7080be5bab1cdd0c6486ea221ca14b5af62`.
Revision 3 was saved and closed. Source revision 8 and manifest
`ae081078c332f9160164fe5836905d14899baf4d00f43c15ab3888517c715a19`
match the original approved check. The full progress snapshot is unchanged.

`desktop-native-codex-live-qz9ebV/retained-reopen-report.json` verifies a new
runtime instance at that same build/source/progress, hashes all native-declared
artifacts before and after, captures an actual formal frame, and saves/closes.
The frame is `formal-563a4aa84d980646f16ef4289271cd64dc8c5699ff1165cb90f84cc1010773b6.png`.
It reports acceleration enabled, platform-default ANGLE, enabled GPU compositing
and WebGL. These are actual runtime graphics diagnostics, not physical-device
identification or traversal acceptance.

The normal desktop already uses platform graphics selection. Its shared host
now also gets bounded startup phase/frame/page diagnostics; no desktop safety
path is bypassed. The single-runtime software checker remains available and
unchanged. `test-results/codex-startup-regression-20260913-01/live-native-report.json`
separately passes real first load, physics movement/save, candidate preview,
fresh application, injected save failure recovery and cold reopen on an
independent newly initialized native world. No live model calls were used.
